title: Aminah at Abwa
hookLine: his mother dies on the road home from Yathrib when he is six

cards: A grown man stops at a grave and weeps, and the people with him weep too. Sahih Muslim keeps the scene. The man is the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and the grave belongs to his mother.
He was a small boy the last time he saw her alive. It happened far from home, on a journey, in a place called Abwa, on the road between Yathrib and Mecca. Today: Aminah.

teach.b: After the boy came back from Halimah's people, he lived with his mother, Aminah, in Mecca.
The sirah says that when he was six, she took him north to Yathrib, the oasis town that would one day be called Medina, to visit relatives there.
With them, the sirah says, went Umm Ayman, a woman of the household who helped care for him.
On the way home, at Abwa, Aminah fell ill and died. She was buried there.
And Umm Ayman brought the boy the rest of the way to Mecca without her. Sit with that road for a moment. His father, Abdullah, had died before he was born, the sirah says.
He never saw his father's face. Now he has seen his mother's for the last time. An orphan twice.
Ibn Ishaq tells it in a few plain sentences, and doesn't dwell. It's the hadith that shows how deep it went.

teach.h: THE GROWN MAN AT THE GRAVE.
teach.b: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet visits his mother's grave and weeps, and he tells the people with him that he asked his Lord for permission to visit it, and permission was given.
Then he says: visit graves, because they remind you of death.
So the grief that began on a road at Abwa becomes, years later, a teaching about remembering. And notice who carried him home. Umm Ayman stays in the story, and Muslims remember her with honor.
A loss, and right beside it, a woman who did not let go of his hand.

how: Muslims who hear of a death say inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un, from surah 2:156, and visiting graves to remember death follows the Prophet's ﷺ words in Sahih Muslim.

s: the Prophet never spoke of his mother again
in Sahih Muslim he visits her grave and weeps.
Umm Ayman brought him back to Mecca
so the sirah says, after Aminah died at Abwa.
at her grave he said: visit graves, they remind you of death

games.q: Aminah has died at Abwa, far from Mecca. a small boy is left with one woman of the household. what happens next?
o: they stay in Yathrib with relatives.
Umm Ayman brings him home to Mecca.
games.why: Umm Ayman carried him the rest of the way to Mecca, the sirah says.

practice: Bring to mind a mother who died young, your own, a friend's, or a woman in a story, and the child she left behind, and hold them both gently without needing to fix anything; if this is too close today, remember Aminah instead, on the road at Abwa.
At news of a death, Muslims say a line from surah two, which Pickthall renders: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning." If you pray, you can say it now; if not, just keep her in mind.

wordCard.voice: Aminah. The Prophet's mother, who died on the road home from Yathrib, the sirah says, and was buried at Abwa while her small son was carried on to Mecca. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: an orphan twice. Tomorrow, the grandfather's rug. Gently, until then.

sources.q: Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.
